questions.stem: What happens to a red blood cell when it is placed in pure water?

options.text: It shrinks and becomes crenated because water leaves by osmosis
It remains the same size because the cell membrane blocks all water movement
It divides into two smaller cells
It swells and eventually bursts (lyses) because water enters by osmosis

questions.explanation: In pure water, the water concentration outside the red blood cell is higher than inside. Water enters the cell by osmosis, causing it to swell. Since animal cells lack a cell wall, there is nothing to prevent them from bursting (lysing).
